approach: Add one shared helper next to `boundary_scan` in athena-context/src/briefs.rs: `plain_boundary_text(text) -> Result<String, String>`. It rewrites each boundary word to a plain alternative (the first list word becomes 'the person running Athena', its plural 'the people running Athena', the others similar plain words). It matches whole words, ignores case and keeps a leading capital. It replaces each boundary fragment (machine paths) with a neutral placeholder. It then re-runs `boundary_scan` and returns an Err naming any term it could not clear. Text with no hit comes back unchanged. Every writer calls it before its text is written. (1) steward.rs: `StewardRequest::new` cleans title, body and acceptance and refuses a file path with a hit; `validate_item` cleans the title and refuses a key with a hit; `blind_spot_change` takes a clean title. (2) hestia.rs: `root_cause_request_at` and `try_error_review` call the helper on the cause and the final text before `self.queue`. (3) introspect.rs: `apply_answer` cleans the four prose fields and the new class name and description after redaction and before the record is built. (4) work_decisions.rs: `approve_request` returns `Result<String>` and cleans the whole built request, because the cited file, job and commit text it copies in is the real source of the 2026-10-29 failure; `approve_work` passes an Err up before `ask`. Tests sit beside each writer, all in athena-core, with boundary words built from fragments. Test names contain 'boundary' (writers) or 'approve_work' (approve-work) so the demonstration filters select them. CHANGELOG gets one entry written without a boundary word.

decisions.choice: One shared sanitiser in athena-context/src/briefs.rs, built on boundary_words, boundary_fragments and boundary_scan and re-verified by a final boundary_scan.
decisions.reason: The fault is that each writer produces text the admission scan rejects. The scan and its word lists live in briefs.rs. Putting the rewrite beside them keeps scan and rewrite in step, and the re-scan means a rewrite can never hand back text that still fails. briefs.rs is a listed deliverable.

rejected.option: Fix only the steward proposal that failed on 2026-10-29
rejected.why: The root-cause default asks for the fault to be fixed at its origin. Hestia and the introspection writer have the same flaw.

rejected.option: Put the helper in steward.rs and have hestia.rs and introspect.rs import it
rejected.why: The list and scan are in athena-context; a helper there is the one place that cannot drift from them.

rejected.option: Only refuse text that has a boundary word, never rewrite
rejected.why: A refused steward proposal is dropped, which is the failure described. Refusal is kept only where a rewrite is unsafe: file paths and keys.

decisions.choice: Clean in `StewardRequest::new` for title, body and acceptance bullets, plus an explicit call in hestia.rs and introspect.rs.
decisions.reason: All steward-channel requests are built through `StewardRequest::new`, so one fix covers steward, root-cause, spec, throughput, backfill and code-health builders. Hestia and introspect still call the helper themselves because the introspection cause enters text before the builder and each file must visibly call the check.

rejected.why: That is the admission scan itself, which is out of scope, and it would reword text the person typed.

decisions.choice: Clean the finished request inside `approve_request` (now `Result<String>`), not only the stored work item.
decisions.reason: The failure came from approve-work. The request copies in the content of every cited file, job and commit, so a clean title can still fail at admission. The only caller is `approve_work`. Old records are not rewritten; the rewrite happens when the request is built.

rejected.option: Clean only the work item title when the steward writes it
rejected.why: It leaves cited-content hits and already stored work items failing.

decisions.choice: Fragments (machine paths) are replaced with a neutral placeholder; keys and file paths with a hit are refused with a message naming the term.
decisions.reason: A key may use only letters, digits and `: _ . / , -`, and a path must stay a real path. A rewrite could make either invalid or change the file named.

rejected.why: It adds a second key grammar and risks key collisions that break de-duplication.

decisions.choice: Criterion 3 is shown by `cargo test --locked` as the primary command, with fmt, clippy and the policy test run as separate simple commands, instead of one chained command.
decisions.reason: The verifier runs whole simple commands, and a chain hides which check failed. The test run carries the behavior: it contains the per-writer and approve-work tests, so it fails when any writer stops cleaning.

rejected.option: One `&&` chain of all four commands
rejected.why: Not a whole simple command; one failure hides the others.

files.purpose: Add `plain_boundary_text` and a fragment-built replacement table next to `boundary_scan`, with unit tests for case, plural, hyphenated forms, fragments, multi-line text, non-ASCII neighbours, an unfixable residue returning Err, and clean text unchanged.

`StewardRequest::new` cleans title, body and acceptance and refuses a path with a hit; `validate_item` cleans the title and refuses a key with a hit; `blind_spot_change` takes a clean title; steward-proposal test.
`root_cause_request_at` and `try_error_review` call the helper on cause and final text before `self.queue`; error-review and root-cause request tests.
`apply_answer` cleans the four prose fields and new class name and description after redaction; on Err sets `record.failure` naming the term; writer test.
`approve_request` returns `Result<String>` and cleans the built text; `approve_work` uses `?`; approve-work test; module doc updated.
Unreleased entry: writers keep boundary words out of proposals, requests and records via one shared check, with no boundary word.

steps: In crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, add a fragment-built table mapping each `boundary_words()` entry to a plain alternative (first list word becomes 'the person running Athena', its plural 'the people running Athena', similar for the rest). Add `pub fn plain_boundary_text(text: &str) -> Result<String, String>`: rewrite whole words case-insensitively, longest first, keep a leading capital, replace fragments with a placeholder, re-run `boundary_scan` and return an Err naming any term left over. Write a doc comment for an outside reader and the unit tests.

In steward.rs, call the helper in `StewardRequest::new` on the title, body and each acceptance bullet, and refuse a file path with a hit with a message naming the term. Do the cleaning before the bullet and path parse checks. In `validate_item`, clean the title and make `check_key` refuse a key with a hit. Update doc comments.

In hestia.rs, clean the cause text and the finished request text in `root_cause_request_at`, and call the helper on the text in `try_error_review` before `self.queue`. Turn an Err into the existing error line.

In introspect.rs `apply_answer`, after `redact_all` and before assignment, clean each prose field and the new class name and description. On Err set `record.failure` naming the term and return None, as the other refusals do.
In work_decisions.rs, make `approve_request` return `Result<String>` and clean the whole built text; have `approve_work` use `?`; update the module doc.

Add tests, named so the filters `boundary` and `approve_work` select them: the steward proposal test, the Hestia error-review and root-cause tests, the introspection writer test, and the approve-work test. Use `athena_context::briefs::boundary_scan` and `crate::reading::scan_request_input` as the oracle, and build the boundary word from fragments.
Add the CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entry naming the root cause and the single shared check, without any boundary word.
Run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked` and `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`, and fix what they report.

risks.risk: A rewrite changes the meaning of a sentence, for example 'lease' becoming 'claim' inside quoted code.
risks.mitigation: Alternatives are chosen to read plainly in general text. The rewrite applies only to text bound for a request or record, and only on a hit. Text with no hit is returned byte for byte, and a test shows this.

risks.risk: A replacement lands next to other words and recreates a boundary word, or a fragment sits across a rewrite.
risks.mitigation: The helper re-runs `boundary_scan` on its output and returns an Err naming the term. Writers turn that Err into a refusal that names the word, so a bad request is never written.

risks.risk: Matching on a lowercase copy gives byte offsets that differ from the original for non-ASCII characters.
risks.mitigation: Use `to_ascii_lowercase`, which keeps byte length. All listed words and fragments are ASCII. Whole-word boundaries are checked on the original characters. A test uses non-ASCII text next to a word.

risks.risk: Changing `approve_request` to return `Result` or `StewardRequest::new` to reword text breaks existing tests that compare exact text.
risks.mitigation: Text with no hit is unchanged. The only caller of `approve_request` is `approve_work`. Run the whole suite (`cargo test --locked`) including athena-cli tests/work_decisions.rs and tests/drain.rs.

risks.risk: A test file or comment holds a boundary word and fails the repository policy scan.
risks.mitigation: Build every word from fragments, as `boundary_words` does. Run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` before finishing. Write the CHANGELOG entry as 'the person running Athena' and do not list the words.

risks.risk: The steward's rewritten title no longer matches its blind-spot key or de-duplication.
risks.mitigation: Keys come from the source name or model key, not the title. Keys with a hit are refused, not rewritten, so a stored key is never changed.

demonstrations.method: Four unit tests, one per writer, each seeded with a boundary word built from fragments (for example `["oper","ator"].concat()`). Each asserts that `athena_context::briefs::boundary_scan` returns no hits on the written text and that the text contains 'the person running Athena'. (a) Steward proposal, steward.rs tests: call `validate_items` with a `StewardItemOutput` whose title and request hold the word, source and evidence from `records_with_job`, then `decide` with `RequestQueue` and a role with a high enough limit; read the queued request from `QueuedRequest.file` and the title from `WorkItem.title`; assert `boundary_scan` and `crate::reading::scan_request_input` (the admission scan) are empty on both; also `decide` with a role below the rung and assert the stored work item title is clean. (b) Hestia error review, hestia.rs tests: `athena_in` and `put`, seed two introspections in different jobs with one class whose cause holds the word, as in `two_introspections_of_one_cause_in_different_jobs...`; call `athena.error_review(&second, &Quiet)`; assert `Some(job)` came back (so `queue` admitted it) and the request text read from `records(&athena)` is clean. (c) Hestia root-cause request: call `root_cause_request(&cause, &records)` on a `RepeatedCause` from `repeated_causes`; assert the returned text is clean. (d) Introspection writer, introspect.rs tests: existing `athena_with(None)`, a `redactor` built from `JobConfig::at(...).config`, an empty `Records::default()` and an `Answer` whose what_happened, cause, prevention and proposed_request hold the word; call `athena.apply_answer(...)`; assert each stored `IntrospectionRecord` field is clean and the status is Recorded. Every seam is an existing function or fixture; the producer confirms reachability of `redactor`, `Records::default` and `apply_answer` from the introspect tests module. Guards: `decide` needs the rung/limit for the role; `error_review` needs two jobs in one class.
demonstrations.observes: Four tests pass, each reporting no boundary_scan hits on the written text and the plain phrase present; (b) also shows the request was admitted.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the `plain_boundary_text` calls removed from the writers, `boundary_scan` finds the word in each written text so each of the four assertions fails; the (b) test also fails because `queue` refuses the request through `refuse_banned_input`.

demonstrations.method: Test in work_decisions.rs `tests` (athena-core). Build a repository with `athena.toml` and `defaults.toml` as the `repo`/`athena_with` helpers in run_pin_tests.rs and hestia.rs do (the producer checks whether `crate::test_support::make_athena` already supplies a reader script). Commit a proposal-kind work item whose source is a committed file, or a cited job, whose text holds a boundary word built from fragments. The `Athena` uses a `FakeAgentDriver` whose reader turn returns a valid reading with a capability registered (an existing seam, used in run_pin_tests.rs); the double only returns a canned reading, and the sanitising logic under test is the production `approve_request`. Call production `athena.approve_work(id, &Quiet)`. First build the raw (unsanitised) text in the test itself and assert it has `boundary_scan` hits, so the seed is shown to trigger the failure.
demonstrations.observes: approve_work returns Ok. The stored job request text has an empty `crate::reading::scan_request_input` and no `boundary_scan` hits, and contains 'the person running Athena'. `crate::reading::check_boundary_and_repo_files(&reading, None)` is Ok on the stored reading. A `WorkDecision` record names the approved job.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the cleaning step in `approve_request`, `approve_work` calls `ask`, which calls `refuse_banned_input` and returns the 'request was not admitted' error; this is the 2026-10-29 failure and the test's unwrap fails.

demonstrations.method: The full test suite, which includes the per-writer tests of criterion 1, the approve-work test of criterion 2, the briefs.rs unit tests of the helper, and the athena-cli tests (work_decisions.rs, drain.rs). The verifier also runs these as separate simple commands: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`. The policy test scans tracked files, including the new tests, helper doc comments, the replacement table and the CHANGELOG entry; all boundary words in them are built from fragments.
demonstrations.observes: All four commands exit 0; no existing test that compares exact text breaks, because text with no hit is returned unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: If a writer stopped cleaning, its per-writer test or the approve-work test inside `cargo test --locked` fails. If a test or the CHANGELOG entry held a literal boundary word, `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` fails. If the helper or its callers were unformatted or left unused or wrongly typed code, fmt or clippy -D warnings fails.

demonstrations.method: Read CHANGELOG.md: the Unreleased section has a bullet saying the writers (the steward and its proposals, Hestia's error review and root-cause requests, the introspection writer, and approve-work) now rewrite boundary words to plain wording before text becomes a request or record, naming the single shared check. The policy scan reads CHANGELOG.md.
demonstrations.observes: The policy test passes, so the entry holds no boundary word; a Grep of CHANGELOG.md for 'boundary' or 'plain' shows the new bullet.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff for calls to the shared helper in the three writer files.
demonstrations.observes: Each file has an added line calling `plain_boundary_text` in a non-test function: steward.rs in `StewardRequest::new` and `validate_item`; hestia.rs in `root_cause_request_at` or `try_error_review`; introspect.rs in `apply_answer`. work_decisions.rs has it in `approve_request`.

open_questions: Does a declined reading commit a job record? If so, the approve-work test can use a minimal fake reader; if not, it needs a registered capability as in run_pin_tests.rs. Check `read_for` and `first_reading` in reading.rs and `test_support::make_athena`.
Are `Athena::redactor`, `Records::default` and `apply_answer` reachable from the `tests` module in introspect.rs? Use `JobConfig::at(&athena.git, &head)?.config` for the redactor config.
Should the placeholder for a machine-path fragment read '[local path]'? Any wording is fine if the re-scan passes.
Does `Redactor::redact` in `queue` bring back a hit? It replaces paths with `<state>`, `<job>` and `~`, which should not add boundary words; test (b) covers it.
